page: Amazon Web Services m5d.xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-virtualized instance built with dedicated compute resources and directly attached high-speed NVMe instance storage. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, offering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration is provisioned with 16 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside a dedicated 150 GB local NVMe SSD volume and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware feature flags include support for AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions.

Benchmark evaluations position the m5d.xlarge primarily in entry to lower-mid compute performance tiers compared across modern cloud infrastructure. Its raw computing capacity produces a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,183.0 and a single-core score of 995.0, with stress-ng recording 3,464.56 multi-core operations per second. PassMark CPU testing yields 4,038.89 points, while PassMark memory scoring reflects stable midrange throughput at 1,897.61 points. Memory bandwidth reaches 187.15 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read blocks and 25.17 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads. In operational scenarios, it achieves 3.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.73 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The integration of local NVMe SSD storage eliminates network latency overhead for temporary file processing and caching layers compared to standard network-attached storage alone. However, compute-bound workloads encounter performance ceilings given the dual-core physical topology and older Cascade Lake microarchitecture. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high utility for applications requiring direct-attached scratch disks without purchasing premium storage instances, though tasks demanding intensive multi-threaded processing or modern AI acceleration may experience diminished throughput efficiency.

The m5d.xlarge is well-matched for mid-tier web serving, intermediate relational and caching databases with low-latency local cache requirements, CI/CD worker nodes, and batch processing workloads that generate substantial ephemeral data.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Supported by 16 GB of DDR4 system memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it incorporates a bundled 150 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume and a 1 Gbps baseline network link. Standard instruction sets include AVX-512F and AES. In benchmark testing, the instance registers a PassMark CPU score of 4,038.89, a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,183.0, and 3.19 million Redis SET operations per second, with memory subsystem benchmarks achieving midrange results. The combination of dedicated compute and integrated high-speed scratch storage makes this instance balanced for web backends, caching services, software builds, and transactional applications requiring low-latency ephemeral storage.
